lots.guide_summary: All evidence is SOLD at Gowans (Feb to Sep 2026); no UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. Sound all-metal 9ct rings of 5.4g to 7.6g hammered $310 to $460, which is $55 to $69 per gram. Scaled to 5.1g that is about $280 to $350 hammer. The closest match, a 7.6g engraved signet, made $450 on 27 Sep 2026 ($59/g, about $302 at 5.1g). All AUD, rate 1. Melt (a floor, not a sale): XAU USD 4103.40 (api.gold-api.com, 2026-10-07) x 1.43284 AUD per USD (open.er-api.com, 2026-10-07) / 31.1035 = AUD 189.0/g pure; x 0.375 = AUD 70.9/g; x 5.1g = about AUD 361.
lots.working: Keep: no identical 5.1g signet has sold, so I adjusted the sound all-metal SOLD entries for weight. The lowest per-gram rate is $330/6g = $55/g (lot 398081, Mar 2026). 5.1g x $55 = $280.50 hammer equivalent. $280.50 / 1.198 = $234.1, rounded down to $230 hammer (all-in about $275.54, about 76% of melt). Flip: likely resale about $300 (Gowans sound-ring rate of $57 to $59/g x 5.1g, or about 83% of the $361 melt from a scrap buyer). Less a 10% selling fee ($30) and no outbound postage (local sale) = $270. $270 / 2.396 = $112.7, rounded down to $110 hammer.
lots.confidence_reason: The 9ct Rodd stamp was read in the photo. At least five sound 9ct all-metal ring sales from the last 12 months were checked in the API, with photos viewed. The weight is Gowans' figure and is not verified.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped lot 402968 ($150, 9ct ring 5.1g size X): same weight and size, but its photo shows a stone-set ring (square brown cabochon), so the weight includes the stone. Not the same item. Dropped lot 363330 ($83, broken Rodd signet with stone missing), lot 416044 ($145, unmarked part signet) and lot 422431 ($160, 9ct part ring 5g): damaged or part pieces, not in comparable condition. They show the scrap downside of about $30/g. Corrected the researcher's price-string slips: lot 363352 is $120, not $125, and for lot 382225 the '$330' text was spurious (the price is $400).
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: yellow gold signet with a shaped shield head engraved with a script monogram (looks like 'JRD' or similar), scroll detail on the shoulders, and a fairly slim shank. Photo 2 (enlarged): the stamp under the head reads '9ct' (worn) over 'Rodd'. Scratches and wear on the head. No visible cracks or solder seams in the two photos, but the back of the shank is not fully shown.
lots.condition: Worn and scratched, with softened engraving. The shank looks slim but intact in the photos. Weight 5.1g and size X per Gowans.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please confirm that lot 9 weighs 5.1g on your scale, and check that the shank is not cracked, very thin or repaired at the back.

lots.guide_summary: All SOLD, all at Gowans, all within the last 10 months. Bundles of the same mid-century Tasmanian labels have made anything from $10 (11 labels including Stork and Top, Aug 2026) to $440 (16 labels including Haven, Sep 2026) and $450. Most ordinary bundles make $14 to $60 hammer, median about $40. Four lots since mid-August made $280 to $450. That looks like a few keen collectors chasing particular lots rather than a reliable price, because results of $10 to $30 happened in the same weeks. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence found. All AUD.
lots.working: Keep: the lowest same-item SOLD price is $10 (lot 434560, 11 similar labels, listed 2026-08-30). $10 / 1.198 = 8.3, rounded down to $5. Flip: likely resale is about $40 (the median for ordinary bundles). Less about 13% fees ($5.20) and $10 postage leaves $24.80, and 24.80 / 2.396 = 10.4, rounded down to $10. The $280 to $450 results are real sales, but they vary too much from lot to lot to set a bid on. Chasing them is a gamble that the same collectors turn up.
lots.confidence_reason: The labels are read clearly in the photos, and I opened many matching SOLD entries and checked their photos. But prices are wildly inconsistent ($10 to $450), so the value cannot be predicted.
lots.condition: The labels look clean, bright and unused, with sharp colours. Minor edge creases are possible. The backs are not shown.
lots.key_photo_findings: Five photos show about 14 labels face up, with a few stacked beneath (Beautiful Isle at least doubled, possibly Top). Brands and packers read: Ideal Pears and Golden Key (W.D. Peacock); Boomerang, Haven, Beautiful Isle, Top Flite and Pinnacle (H. Jones & Co); Huonery (Port Huon Fruitgrowers Co-op); Bright Star (T.E. Butler); Top (Tasmanian Orchardists & Producers); Stork (Clements & Marshall); A. Port Pty Ltd; and Tas Fruit Cat. 1 (later and plainer).

Flip: likely resale about $96 (what Gowans buyers paid all-in for the plain 35.8g band, $80 x 1.198), sold on eBay at about 13% fees and $10 tracked postage: 96 x 0.87 - 10 = 73.5; 73.5 / 2.396 = 30.7, round down = $30 hammer.
